chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Ali ibn Hadid, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A water-skin containing water, into which a dead mouse, rat, or sparrow fell. He said: “If it decomposed in it, then do not drink from its water and do not perform wudu (ablution) with it, and pour it out. But if it is not decomposed, then drink from it and perform wudu (ablution) from it, and cast away the carcass when you remove it while it is fresh. And likewise the jar, the water vessel, the waterskin, and similar containers of water.”

He said: And Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: “If the water is more than a water-skin, nothing that decomposes in it or does not decompose renders it impure, unless there comes to it an odor that overcomes the smell of the water.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report can be understood such that his saying “a water-skin of water” refers to when its amount is a kurr; for when it is like that, whatever falls into it does not render it impure. And his saying, “if it decomposed in it, then do not drink and do not perform wudu (ablution),” is to be understood as referring to when one of the qualities of the water changes. Likewise is the statement regarding the jar, the water vessel, and the waterskin. No one may say that the jar, the vessel, and the waterskin cannot hold a kurr of water, because the report does not state that a single jar has that ruling; rather, it mentioned them with the definite article, and that indicates generality according to many of the people of language. If that is possible, then it does not conflict with the reports we mentioned earlier.

key_terms.الْمَيْتَةَ: the dead carcass of the animal
key_terms.تَفَسَّخَ: decomposed or disintegrated in the water
key_terms.رَاوِيَةٌ: a waterskin or large water container
key_terms.رِيحٌ: an odor or smell affecting the water
key_terms.كُرًّا: the legal measure of a large quantity of water
key_terms.لَا تَتَوَضَّأْ: do not perform wudu (ablution) with it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on water if a dead mouse or similar animal falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal rulings of water when a dead animal falls into it, distinguishing between decomposed and non-decomposed carcasses and between lesser and greater quantities of water. It also includes Shaykh al-Tusi's reconciliation of the report with other narrations by interpreting the ruling in light of the measure of kurr and changes in the water's properties.
